gives.name: w
gives.what: minimum size of a fillet weld, as its leg dimension

takes.name: t
takes.what: material thickness of the thinner part joined

gives.name: Fn
gives.what: nominal stress of a fastener: the tensile stress Fnt, or the shear stress Fnv in a bearing-type connection

takes.name: fastener
takes.what: description of the fastener, one name for each line that holds numbers

takes.name: stress
takes.what: which stress: tensile, shear with threads not excluded from the shear planes (N), shear with threads excluded from the shear planes (X)

gives.name: dh
gives.what: nominal diameter of a standard or an oversize hole

gives.name: le
gives.what: minimum edge distance from the centre of a standard hole to the edge of the connected part

not_written.what: The metric value printed in parentheses after each inch value: band ends 6, 13 and 19 mm, and sizes 3, 5, 6 and 8 mm.
not_written.why: A band end or a cell holds one value. The inch value is transcribed; the mm value is a second, rounded number in the same place.

not_written.what: Footnote [a] on the size column: the size is the leg dimension, and a weld made with electrodes that are not low-hydrogen must be single pass. Also the note that points to J2.2b for the maximum size.
not_written.why: A requirement on the welding process, not a value. A row cannot hold a condition that is not a comparison of quantities. The cells are unchanged by it.

not_written.what: The sixth line, threaded parts meeting Section A3.4: Fnt = 0.75 Fu, Fnv (N) = 0.450 Fu, Fnv (X) = 0.563 Fu.
not_written.why: A formula in place of a number: each cell reads Fu, which the row does not take. The line is left out, so the key `fastener` has five names, for the first five lines in order.

not_written.what: The MPa value printed in parentheses in each cell, by line: 310, 190, 190; 620, 370, 470; 750, 450, 560; 780, 470, 580; 1000, 620, 780.
not_written.why: Two numbers in one cell. The ksi value is transcribed.

not_written.what: Footnote [c] on both Fnv columns: in an end-loaded connection whose fastener pattern is longer than 38 in. (950 mm), Fnv is 83.3% of the tabulated value.
not_written.why: A footnote that changes the value under a condition. The condition reads a pattern length and a connection type that the row does not take. The plain values are transcribed.

not_written.what: Footnote [d] on the two shear cells of the A307 line: the value is reduced by 1% for each 1/16 in. (2 mm) of grip length over five diameters.
not_written.why: A footnote that changes the value under a condition, reading a grip length and a diameter that the row does not take. The plain value, 27 ksi, is transcribed.

not_written.what: Footnote [b] on the Fnt column: the tensile strength may instead be taken as the tensile stress area times the specified minimum tensile stress of the material; the tabulated values assume a tensile stress area of 0.75 times the gross area.
not_written.why: A permitted alternative method, not a value of the table.

not_written.what: Footnotes [a], [e] and [f]: [a] on Fnt sends high-strength bolts under tensile fatigue to Appendix 3; [e] on column N says threads are assumed and permitted in the shear planes in all cases; [f] on the two shear cells of the Group 200 line says the transition area of those bolts counts as threaded.
not_written.why: Conditions of use that are not comparisons of quantities. They change no printed value.

not_written.what: The last line, bolt diameter 1 1/8 in. and over: standard d + 1/8, oversize d + 5/16.
not_written.why: A formula in place of a number, and a line for a range of diameters in a table otherwise given at listed sizes. The line is left out; the row stops at 1 in.

not_written.what: The short-slot and long-slot columns, width x length. Short-slot by line: 9/16 x 11/16, 11/16 x 7/8, 13/16 x 1, 15/16 x 1 1/8, 1 1/8 x 1 5/16, (d + 1/8) x (d + 3/8). Long-slot by line: 9/16 x 1 1/4, 11/16 x 1 9/16, 13/16 x 1 7/8, 15/16 x 2 3/16, 1 1/8 x 2 1/2, (d + 1/8) x 2.5 d.
not_written.why: Two numbers in one cell, as tables.tsv says.

not_written.what: The last line, bolt diameter over 1 1/4 in.: 1 1/4 times d.
not_written.why: A formula in place of a number. The line is left out; the row stops at 1 1/4 in.

not_written.what: Footnote [a] on the title: a lesser edge distance is permitted where Sections J3.11 and J4 are satisfied, but one under a bolt diameter needs the engineer of record's approval. Footnote [b]: for an oversized or slotted hole see Table J3.5.
not_written.why: A permission that lowers the minimum under conditions that are not comparisons of quantities, and a pointer to another table. The printed values are transcribed as they stand.
